bottleneck: Every Parkinson's therapy treats symptoms — dopamine replacement, DBS — while neurons keep dying. Alpha-synuclein antibodies, the leading disease-modifying bet, have failed to slow progression in trials, and it is unclear whether synuclein aggregation causes or follows neurodegeneration. By diagnosis, most dopaminergic neurons are already lost, so even a perfect drug may arrive too late, and no validated prodromal biomarker enables earlier intervention.
current_state: No disease-modifying Parkinson's therapy exists. Research is shifting to earlier detection and alternative targets, but the causal chain from synuclein to cell death is still disputed.
title: No disease-modifying Parkinson's therapy
why_it_blocks: Symptomatic treatment while the brain degenerates is a holding action, not medicine. Without a way to stop neuronal loss — and to detect the disease before the loss — Parkinson's remains a managed decline.
